ops.title: apple/container virtiofs idmap: uid model for hermes-agent OCI
ops.body:
Empirically measured live 2026-07-18 during the container-native hermes bring-up (crash-loop diagnosis). Governs the agent-identity + sandbox-socket model.

## The idmap
apple/container bind mounts (virtiofs) map the **host owner (login uid 501) → guest `root:root` (0:0)**; the host GROUP does not survive either (a host gid-1000 file/socket shows guest gid 0). Original mode is preserved.

## Access asymmetry (the whole story)
- **Regular FILE read/write is HOST-enforced, not guest-DAC-enforced.** Guest uid 1000 reads/writes ANY bind-mounted file/dir regardless of cosmetic mode/owner (confirmed: uid 1000 read a root:root mode-600 secret and wrote a root:root mode-700 dir), because host-side virtiofsd (uid 501) owns everything with full perms. So the uid-1000 drop provides **zero secret/state confidentiality** on the bind mount.
- **`chown` in the guest**: silent NO-OP on files (rc=0, guest view unchanged); HARD ERROR "Operation not permitted" on the bind-mount ROOT inode. Any `chown -R <bindmount>` under `set -e` crashes PID 1 (this was BUG 1).
- **Unix SOCKET `connect()` IS guest-DAC-enforced** against the cosmetic view. The proxy socket (host `501:1000 660`) shows guest `root:root 660`: guest root connects; uid1000/gid1000 → EACCES; uid1000 **+ supplementary group 0** → connects. (This was BUG 2 / "sup #2".)

## Decisions (user-approved 2026-07-18)
- **FIX 1**: delete the entrypoint `chown -R $HERMES_STATE_DIR` (impossible + unnecessary).
- **Socket access = Option D**: dropped agent runs `setpriv --reuid=1000 --regid=1000 --groups=1000,0 --no-new-privs`. Group 0 = guest's root group (the mapped host user). Enumeration of the minimal image confirmed group 0 unlocks NOTHING on the local rootfs (no group-0 group-writable files, no local sockets, no setuid/setgid) beyond the intended proxy socket. Host socket stays `660 gid-1000` in dir `2750 gid-1000` — host-side restriction fully intact.
- Rejected B (run-as-root: loses capability restriction for no gain). Deferred G (socket 666 + dir gate: a second host artifact to keep in sync).
- **Supervisor canary** must exec as root then `setpriv` to the EXACT prod creds (uid1000,gid1000,+group0) — a bare `--user 1000:1000` tests the socket ACL (EACCES), not the proxy's 403 filtering (codex Q3b).

## Rationale correction
The uid-1000 drop's value is NOT file/secret isolation (idmap defeats it) — it is **capability restriction + `--no-new-privs` + in-VM process isolation** (guest-kernel-enforced, untouched by the idmap). Real boundary = the micro-VM + the filtering proxy; untrusted code runs only in nested sandboxes, never the agent container. Stop asserting "the drop protects secrets".

## Follow-up (non-blocking, codex Q4-8)
True secret-confidentiality-from-a-compromised-agent needs an architectural fix (host-side read-only VM mount flag, or decrypt-on-demand via a proxy instead of materializing secret files), not a uid choice.

Precedent note: hermes-agent ran for months in the tart VM against a host-user-owned virtiofs state dir, so it does NOT gate loading on file ownership — FIX 1 is safe on that axis.
